cues.en: I have a couple of questions for you — but they’re personal.
cues.zh: 我想问大家几个问题——不过这些问题比较私人。

cues.en: So I’m not going to ask for a show of hands.
cues.zh: 所以我就不请大家举手了。

cues.en: First, right now, at this stage of your life, are you lonely?
cues.zh: 第一，就在此刻，在你人生的这个阶段，你孤独吗？

cues.en: And if not, have you ever been lonely?
cues.zh: 如果不孤独，那你曾经孤独过吗？

cues.en: My favorite description of loneliness comes from Zoë Heller's book "Notes on a Scandal."
cues.zh: 我最喜欢的一段关于孤独的描述，出自佐伊·海勒的小说《丑闻笔记》。

cues.en: And in it, the narrator, who is played in the movie by Judi Dench,
cues.zh: 书中的叙述者——在电影里由朱迪·丹奇饰演——

cues.en: distinguishes between passing loneliness and something deeper.
cues.zh: 区分了一时的孤独和某种更深层的孤独。

cues.en: So she observes that people think they know what it's like to be lonely.
cues.zh: 她说，人们以为自己知道孤独是什么滋味。

cues.en: You know, they had a bad breakup or a rough time in summer camp.
cues.zh: 你知道的，比如经历过一次糟糕的分手，或者在夏令营里过得不太顺。

cues.en: But then she says this.
cues.zh: 但接着她这样说：

cues.en: "About the drip, drip of long-haul, no-end-in-sight solitude, they know nothing.
cues.zh: “对于那种日复一日、漫长无尽、看不到尽头的孤寂，他们一无所知。

cues.en: They don't know what it is to construct an entire weekend around a visit to the launderette,
cues.zh: 他们不懂什么叫围绕一趟自助洗衣店之行来安排整个周末，

cues.en: or to sit in a darkened flat on Halloween night, because you can't bear to expose your bleak evening
cues.zh: 也不懂什么叫在万圣节之夜坐在漆黑的公寓里，因为你无法忍受把自己凄凉的夜晚

cues.en: to a crowd of jeering trick-or-treaters."
cues.zh: 暴露在一群起哄讨糖的孩子面前。”

cues.en: And she concludes with this: “I have sat on park benches and trains and school room chairs
cues.zh: 最后她这样总结：“我曾坐在公园长椅上、火车上、教室的椅子上，

cues.en: feeling the great store of unused, objectless love
cues.zh: 感受着那满满的、无处安放、没有对象的爱，

cues.en: sitting in my belly like a stone until I was sure I would cry out and fall, flailing to the ground."
cues.zh: 像石头一样压在我的心底，直到我确信自己会大喊出来，然后倒下，在地上挣扎。”

cues.en: I like this quote for a few reasons.
cues.zh: 我喜欢这段话，有几个原因。

cues.en: It talks about solitude, and solitude is a big source of loneliness, but it also talks about love.
cues.zh: 它讲到了独处，而独处是孤独的一大来源，但它也讲到了爱。

cues.en: You could be with somebody, but if you're not loved, not needed, not respected, you might feel lonely.
cues.zh: 你可能身边有人陪着，但如果你不被爱、不被需要、不被尊重，你仍可能感到孤独。

cues.en: And then there's understanding.
cues.zh: 然后是“被理解”。

cues.en: Suppose you have something in your head that's important to you,
cues.zh: 假设你脑子里有一件对你很重要的事，

cues.en: that matters a lot to you, but you feel others don't get it,
cues.zh: 它对你意义重大，但你觉得别人不理解，

cues.en: or don't care to get it, or aren't trying hard enough to get it.
cues.zh: 或者不在乎去理解，或者不够努力去理解。

cues.en: This too could cause loneliness.
cues.zh: 这同样会让人感到孤独。

cues.en: Loneliness ravages the body as well as the soul.
cues.zh: 孤独摧残的不只是灵魂，还有身体。

cues.en: A report by the Surgeon General associates it with greater risk of cardiovascular disease,
cues.zh: 美国卫生局局长的一份报告指出，孤独与更高的心血管疾病风险相关，

cues.en: dementia, stroke and the like.
cues.zh: 还有痴呆、中风等等。

cues.en: It's the equivalent of smoking 15 cigarettes a day.
cues.zh: 它的危害相当于每天抽 15 支烟。

cues.en: Studies in the United States [and] United Kingdom find that about one in five people
cues.zh: 美国和英国的研究发现，大约每五个人中就有一个

cues.en: describe themselves as often or always lonely.
cues.zh: 说自己经常或总是感到孤独。

cues.en: And the most at-risk group is young adults.
cues.zh: 而风险最高的群体是年轻人。

cues.en: I'm here to talk about a possible cure for loneliness and what it might mean.
cues.zh: 我今天想谈谈孤独的一种可能的“解药”，以及它可能意味着什么。

cues.en: And I think we could see loneliness as similar to boredom.
cues.zh: 我认为，我们可以把孤独看作和无聊类似的东西。

cues.en: I'm old enough to remember when people were bored all the time.
cues.zh: 我年纪够大，还记得人们一天到晚都很无聊的年代。

cues.en: Long train rides, long car rides, long plane rides.
cues.zh: 长途火车、长途开车、长途飞行。

cues.en: Late at night when the TV stations switched off and you were all alone, and you had to read.
cues.zh: 深夜电视台都停播了，你孤零零一个人，只能看书。

cues.en: (Laughter) But now most of us carry around our phones
cues.zh: （笑声）但现在，我们大多数人都随身带着手机，

cues.en: and those phones offer podcasts and movies and books and music and social media and so on.
cues.zh: 这些手机提供播客、电影、书籍、音乐、社交媒体等等。

cues.en: And so for many of us, boredom is a thing of the past.
cues.zh: 所以对我们很多人来说，无聊已经成了过去式。

cues.en: Well the cure for loneliness may also be found in our phones and our laptops.
cues.zh: 而孤独的解药，或许也能在我们的手机和笔记本电脑里找到。

cues.en: And it is, of course, generative AI.
cues.zh: 那当然就是生成式 AI。

cues.en: Last year, some friends and I wrote an article called "In Praise of Empathic AI."
cues.zh: 去年，我和几个朋友写了一篇文章，叫《为有共情力的 AI 说句好话》。

cues.en: If that title makes you cringe and makes you kind of angry, you're not alone.
cues.zh: 如果这个标题让你觉得别扭、甚至有点生气，你并不孤单。

cues.en: Our colleagues hated it.
cues.zh: 我们的同行都很讨厌它。

cues.en: It's the article that I've written that most people hated.
cues.zh: 在我写过的文章里，这是招人讨厌最多的一篇。

cues.en: But bear with me.
cues.zh: 不过请耐心听我说完。

cues.en: We started by making a sort of simple point, which is [to] review a set of studies that have involved —
cues.zh: 我们首先提出了一个很简单的观点，就是回顾了一系列研究，这些研究——

cues.en: like, you get a whole lot of people interacting with other people,
cues.zh: 比如说，让很多人和其他人互动，

cues.en: sometimes doctors, sometimes therapists, sometimes just regular people.
cues.zh: 有时是医生，有时是心理治疗师，有时只是普通人。

cues.en: And you get a whole lot of people interacting with chatbots.
cues.zh: 再让很多人和聊天机器人互动。

cues.en: And then you ask them later: “How did it go, what’s your experience?”
cues.zh: 之后问他们：“感觉怎么样？你的体验如何？”

cues.en: And people tend to rate the chatbots as more empathic, more caring, more understanding.
cues.zh: 结果人们往往认为聊天机器人更有共情力、更体贴、更善解人意。

cues.en: And it's no surprise.
cues.zh: 这一点也不奇怪。

cues.en: AIs are built to be attentive, to be present, to be interested.
cues.zh: AI 本来就被设计成专注、在场、对你感兴趣。

cues.en: An AI is never going to impatiently wait for you to finish telling your story,
cues.zh: AI 永远不会不耐烦地等你讲完你的故事，

cues.en: so it can tell you one of its own.
cues.zh: 好让它讲一个它自己的。

cues.en: (Laughter) An AI is never going to say, "Dude, I'm busy. Get back to me later. I got things going on."
cues.zh: （笑声）AI 永远不会说：“哥们儿，我正忙着呢。回头再找我，我这儿有事。”

cues.en: Suppose some future — I don't think it's happening now,
cues.zh: 假设在将来——我不认为现在已经是这样，

cues.en: but some future AI could serve as a cure for loneliness.
cues.zh: 但假设将来某种 AI 能够成为孤独的解药。

cues.en: Would this be a good thing?
cues.zh: 这会是件好事吗？

cues.en: Well to some extent, yes.
cues.zh: 嗯，在某种程度上，是的。

cues.en: Obviously, yes.
cues.zh: 显然是的。

cues.en: Think about the many millions of elderly people, many in institutions,
cues.zh: 想想那数以百万计的老人，其中很多住在养老机构里，

cues.en: who go for days and nights without talking to anybody, in perfect agony of isolation.
cues.zh: 他们几天几夜都没人说话，承受着彻底与世隔绝的痛苦。

cues.en: Many of them have dementia.
cues.zh: 他们中很多人患有痴呆。

cues.en: Many of them are difficult to interact with for other reasons.
cues.zh: 很多人由于其他原因，也很难与人交流。

cues.en: They don't have family and friends to spend time with them.
cues.zh: 他们没有家人和朋友陪伴。

cues.en: And there's not enough money in the world to pay people to come and talk to them for hours on end.
cues.zh: 而全世界也没有足够的钱，去雇人来陪他们一连聊上好几个小时。

cues.en: If some future version of Chat or Claude or Gemini
cues.zh: 如果未来某个版本的 ChatGPT、Claude 或 Gemini

cues.en: could ease these people's suffering, it would be a godsend.
cues.zh: 能减轻这些人的痛苦，那将是天赐之福。

cues.en: But for the rest of us, it's more complicated.
cues.zh: 但对我们其他人来说，事情就复杂多了。

cues.en: And you can view these cures for loneliness as akin to a powerful painkiller.
cues.zh: 你可以把这些孤独的解药看作一种强效止痛药。

cues.en: Like a powerful painkiller, it can alleviate suffering.
cues.zh: 就像强效止痛药一样，它能减轻痛苦。

cues.en: But like a powerful painkiller, [it] can sometimes come at a terrible cost.
cues.zh: 但也像强效止痛药一样，它有时会带来可怕的代价。

cues.en: And to make sense of the cost, you have to think about what loneliness is for.
cues.zh: 要理解这种代价，你得先想想孤独究竟有什么用。

cues.en: So the neuroscientist John Cacioppo, who founded the modern science of loneliness,
cues.zh: 神经科学家约翰·卡乔波开创了现代孤独研究，

cues.en: argued that it's a biological signal akin to hunger, thirst and pain.
cues.zh: 他认为孤独是一种生物信号，类似于饥饿、口渴和疼痛。

cues.en: And as such, it does two things for us.
cues.zh: 正因如此，它为我们做了两件事。

cues.en: It could sometimes be paralyzing, but when it works out well,
cues.zh: 它有时可能让人陷入瘫痪，但当它发挥正常作用时，

cues.en: it has certain evolved functions that improve our lives.
cues.zh: 它具有一些经过进化而来的功能，能改善我们的生活。

cues.en: So one, just as hunger motivates us to seek out food, loneliness and other forms of social suffering
cues.zh: 第一，就像饥饿促使我们去寻找食物一样，孤独和其他形式的社交痛苦

cues.en: motivate us to seek out and maintain social connection.
cues.zh: 促使我们去寻求并维系社会联系。

cues.en: Because we get lonely, we accept an invitation to a party, we invite a friend out to brunch,
cues.zh: 因为会感到孤独，我们才会接受派对邀请、约朋友出去吃早午餐、

cues.en: we open up the dating apps.
cues.zh: 打开约会软件。

cues.en: It also helps us regulate relationships.
cues.zh: 它还帮助我们调节人际关系。

cues.en: It helps us try to repair a relationship gone wrong, to apologize for messing up,
cues.zh: 它促使我们去修复出了问题的关系，为自己搞砸的事情道歉，

cues.en: to try to show genuine interest in our relationship with somebody else.
cues.zh: 努力对与他人的关系表现出真正的关心。

cues.en: A second thing that loneliness does is it helps us grow as people.
cues.zh: 孤独的第二个作用，是帮助我们成长。

cues.en: It's a truism in psychology that we learn from failure.
cues.zh: 心理学里有一条老生常谈：我们从失败中学习。

cues.en: They call it trial-and-error learning, [or] reinforcement learning.
cues.zh: 这被称为试错学习，或者强化学习。

cues.en: The idea is nicely summed up in the movie "Batman Begins,"
cues.zh: 电影《蝙蝠侠：侠影之谜》把这个道理概括得很好，

cues.en: where young Bruce Wayne’s father asks the future Batman, “Why do we fall?”
cues.zh: 年幼的布鲁斯·韦恩的父亲问这位未来的蝙蝠侠：“我们为什么会跌倒？”

cues.en: And he answers, "So we can learn to pick ourselves up."
cues.zh: 他回答：“为了学会自己爬起来。”

cues.en: This is literally true for toddlers who learn to walk by falling and stumbling and doing things wrong.
cues.zh: 对蹒跚学步的孩子来说，这简直就是字面意义上的真理：他们正是在跌倒、踉跄、犯错中学会走路的。

cues.en: It's true for a comedian who learns to improve her act by bombing on stage, by having her jokes fall flat.
cues.zh: 对喜剧演员也是如此：她靠在台上冷场、靠段子没人笑，来改进自己的表演。

cues.en: It's true for a boxer who learns to evade a punch by getting repeatedly smacked in the face.
cues.zh: 对拳击手也是如此：他靠一次次脸上挨揍，学会躲避出拳。

cues.en: Well failure in a social realm is associated with loneliness.
cues.zh: 而在社交领域，失败就伴随着孤独。

cues.en: And can you imagine what it would be like if people never got [the] signal [of] failure?
cues.zh: 你能想象，如果人们永远收不到失败的信号，会是什么样子吗？

cues.en: Imagine a teenage boy who never learned to cut short his monologues
cues.zh: 想象一个十几岁的男孩，从来没学会适可而止地结束自己的长篇大论，

cues.en: because his AI companion never got bored.
cues.zh: 因为他的 AI 伙伴从来不会觉得无聊。

cues.en: (Laughter) Imagine an adult who never learned to apologize
cues.zh: （笑声）想象一个成年人，从来没学会道歉，

cues.en: because her AI companion never needed an apology.
cues.zh: 因为她的 AI 伙伴从来不需要道歉。

cues.en: Imagine a world where the answer to the question, "Am I the asshole?"
cues.zh: 想象一个世界，在那里，“我是不是个混蛋？”这个问题的答案

cues.en: is always a firm and resounding no.
cues.zh: 永远是坚定而响亮的“不是”。

cues.en: (Laughter and Applause)
cues.zh: （笑声和掌声）

cues.en: Now you might think this has an easy technological fix.
cues.zh: 你可能会觉得，这在技术上很容易解决。

cues.en: You could just go into the settings and make it less sycophantic.
cues.zh: 你只要进入设置，让它少拍点马屁就行了。

cues.en: And in fact, I don't use AI myself for social purposes, but I use it a lot for my work.
cues.zh: 事实上，我自己并不用 AI 来社交，但我工作中经常用它。

cues.en: And after a while I got tired of Chat and Claude just saying,
cues.zh: 用了一段时间后，我厌倦了 ChatGPT 和 Claude 老是说：

cues.en: "Oh, brilliant question, Paul. Oh, oh, such a clever idea.
cues.zh: “哦，保罗，这个问题问得太精彩了。哦，哦，多么聪明的想法。

cues.en: How do you get to be so intelligent?"
cues.zh: 你怎么会这么聪明？”

cues.en: So I went into the settings, and I said, “Stop.
cues.zh: 于是我进入设置，写道：“停。

cues.en: Do not praise me. Be blunt.
cues.zh: 不要夸我。说话直接点。

cues.en: Just be honest. Tell it like it is.”
cues.zh: 实话实说就好，是什么就说什么。”

cues.en: Then a month later, I changed it back.
cues.zh: 结果一个月后，我又改回去了。

cues.en: (Laughter and Applause)
cues.zh: （笑声和掌声）

cues.en: I kind of missed it.
cues.zh: 我有点想念那些夸奖了。

cues.en: (Laughter) You can call this Cordelia's Problem.
cues.zh: （笑声）你可以把这称为“考狄利娅难题”。

cues.en: In Shakespeare's "King Lear," the king brings together his three daughters
cues.zh: 在莎士比亚的《李尔王》中，国王把他的三个女儿召集到一起，

cues.en: to try to decide how to divide up the kingdom, and he has his daughters tell him how much they love him.
cues.zh: 想决定如何分割王国，于是他让女儿们说说她们有多爱他。

cues.en: And his first two daughters praise him.
cues.zh: 前两个女儿对他极尽赞美。

cues.en: They love him infinitely. He's the center of their lives.
cues.zh: 她们说对他的爱无边无际，他是她们生命的中心。

cues.en: Then Cordelia comes up and says, "I love you like a daughter should love her father,
cues.zh: 然后考狄利娅上前说：“我爱您，就像一个女儿应当爱她的父亲那样，

cues.en: no more, no less."
cues.zh: 不多也不少。”

cues.en: The king is enraged and banishes her from the kingdom.
cues.zh: 国王勃然大怒，把她逐出了王国。

cues.en: Now "King Lear" is a tragedy.
cues.zh: 《李尔王》是一出悲剧。

cues.en: His two sycophantic daughters didn't love him at all, and they betray him in the end.
cues.zh: 他那两个阿谀奉承的女儿根本不爱他，最后还背叛了他。

cues.en: Now some of you are probably thinking, “Well, I’m not like King Lear.
cues.zh: 现在你们有些人可能在想：“嗯，我可不像李尔王。

cues.en: I like pushback.
cues.zh: 我喜欢有人反驳我。

cues.en: I don't want that sort of sucking up."
cues.zh: 我不想要那种拍马屁。”

cues.en: And maybe, maybe.
cues.zh: 也许吧，也许吧。

cues.en: But I think some of us like the performance of pushback rather than pushback itself.
cues.zh: 但我觉得，我们中有些人喜欢的是“反驳的表演”，而不是真正的反驳。

cues.en: So yeah, something that always says, "Yes, you're wonderful" gets a bit cloying.
cues.zh: 所以没错，一个永远只会说“对，你真棒”的东西，确实会让人有点腻。

cues.en: But a properly attuned AI won't do that.
cues.zh: 但一个调校得当的 AI 不会那样做。

cues.en: It will resist, it will argue against you, it'll push back.
cues.zh: 它会抵抗，会和你争论，会反驳你。

cues.en: And then finally, in a very satisfying way, [it’ll] say, "I guess you win. You've totally persuaded me."
cues.zh: 然后最后，以一种非常令人满足的方式说：“好吧，算你赢了。你完全说服我了。”

cues.en: And I worry that this sort of intelligent and titrated sycophancy
cues.zh: 我担心的是，这种聪明的、拿捏好分寸的奉承，

cues.en: is more corrosive to the soul than a sort of sucking up yes-men AIs we deal with now.
cues.zh: 比我们现在遇到的那种只会拍马屁、唯唯诺诺的 AI，对灵魂的侵蚀更大。

cues.en: For some of you, the solution will be clear.
cues.zh: 对你们中的一些人来说，解决办法很清楚：

cues.en: Treat these hypersocial AIs like the powerful painkillers they are.
cues.zh: 把这些“超社交”的 AI 当作强效止痛药来对待——它们本来就是。

cues.en: Make them available to the people who need them the most
cues.zh: 只提供给最需要它们的人，

cues.en: and forbid their use for the rest of us.
cues.zh: 而禁止我们其他人使用。

cues.en: But this is not the solution that I believe in.
cues.zh: 但我并不认同这个办法。

cues.en: I'm not a catastrophist when it comes to AI.
cues.zh: 在 AI 问题上，我不是灾难论者。

cues.en: Just like there are people who deal with AI companions in a normal way and benefit from it,
cues.zh: 就像有些人以正常的方式使用 AI 伙伴并从中受益，

cues.en: and it doesn’t harm their life.
cues.zh: 而且这并没有伤害他们的生活。

cues.en: In the same way there are people who resist technological temptations more generally,
cues.zh: 同样，也有人更普遍地能抵挡住科技的诱惑，

cues.en: people who, when faced with the unholy trinity of TikTok, Pornhub and Wordle,
cues.zh: 这些人在面对 TikTok、Pornhub 和 Wordle 这“邪恶三位一体”时，

cues.en: nonetheless — (Laughter) go to the gym, meet with friends, touch grass.
cues.zh: 依然——（笑声）去健身房、和朋友见面、走出门去接接地气。

cues.en: The second reason I don't want to ban these things is more personal.
cues.zh: 我不想禁止这些东西的第二个原因，更私人一些。

cues.en: When I was 11, my mother died of cancer.
cues.zh: 我 11 岁时，母亲因癌症去世。

cues.en: I then entered a period of great pain and then problems with social relationships
cues.zh: 之后我经历了一段非常痛苦的时期，接着是人际关系上的种种问题，

cues.en: and then a period of loneliness that lasted for years.
cues.zh: 然后是持续了好几年的孤独。

cues.en: I would have benefited so much from someone, or find something, that would listen to me,
cues.zh: 如果当时有某个人，或者某样东西，能听我说话，

cues.en: that would express interest, that I could talk to, that I could share my feelings with.
cues.zh: 能对我表现出兴趣，能让我倾诉、和我分享感受，我会受益匪浅。

cues.en: It seems like a betrayal of my past self to say,
cues.zh: 如果我现在说

cues.en: "Tough, do without, suffer and learn from your suffering."
cues.zh: “忍着吧，没有就没有，去受苦，从痛苦中学习”，那就像是背叛了过去的自己。

cues.en: I wonder if the best of all possible worlds is to create imperfect companions,
cues.zh: 我在想，在所有可能的世界中，最好的那个是否是去创造不完美的伙伴——

cues.en: companions that somehow alleviate the pain of loneliness without destroying our humanity.
cues.zh: 这些伙伴能以某种方式减轻孤独的痛苦，却不会摧毁我们的人性。

cues.en: Companions that are difficult enough to deal with that we learn from interacting with them.
cues.zh: 这些伙伴足够难相处，让我们能从与它们的互动中学到东西。

cues.en: Companions that are sufficiently imperfect that we ultimately abandon them to deal with people.
cues.zh: 这些伙伴足够不完美，让我们最终离开它们，去和真实的人打交道。

cues.en: Now I'm pretty confident we could build such things.
cues.zh: 我相当有信心，我们能造出这样的东西。

cues.en: I'm less confident that there's money to be had by doing so.
cues.zh: 但我不太确定，这样做能不能赚到钱。

cues.en: I accept that it might be a bad business model to create AIs that users ultimately outgrow,
cues.zh: 我承认，打造一种用户最终会“毕业”离开的 AI，可能是个糟糕的商业模式，

cues.en: but I hope there are people who care enough to do it anyway.
cues.zh: 但我希望，会有人足够在乎，愿意去做这件事。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家。

cues.en: (Applause)
cues.zh: （掌声）
